slides.say: Maya and Theo start at the same time from opposite ends of a bike trail, and ride toward each other. Theo rides at one point two five times Maya's speed. What fraction of the trail does Maya cover before they meet?
So there's no distance, no time, and no real speed. They only tell us that Theo is one and a quarter times as fast.
We'll solve it in three different ways. First by understanding, with ratio parts, like in the lesson.
They start together, and they stop together when they meet. So the time is fixed, and the distances follow the speeds. The speeds are one to one point two five.
at: The speeds are one to one point two five

slides.say: One point two five is one and a quarter. So we multiply both by four, to make them whole. That's four to five.
So we cut the trail into four plus five, nine equal parts.
Maya rides four parts, and Theo rides five. So Maya covers four out of nine, four ninths of the trail.
[pause] Now let's plug in numbers. We start again from the givens. Data is missing, so we choose friendly numbers.
Let's say Maya rides at sixteen kilometers per hour. We pick sixteen, because a quarter of sixteen is four. So Theo rides at sixteen plus four, twenty.
at: Let's say Maya rides at sixteen

slides.say: Let's say they meet after one hour, the simplest time. The time is the same for both, so any time works.
In that hour, Maya rides sixteen kilometers, and Theo rides twenty. So the trail is sixteen plus twenty, thirty-six kilometers.
Maya covers sixteen out of thirty-six. We divide both by four, and that's four ninths again.
[pause] Now by understanding, with no calculation at all. We start again from the givens. Theo is faster, so Maya covers less than half of the trail.
at: so Maya covers less than half

slides.say: So one half is out. And five ninths is more than half, so it's out too.
Now imagine Theo were exactly twice as fast. Then Maya would cover one part out of three, a third.
at: imagine Theo were exactly twice as fast

slides.say: But Theo is only one and a quarter times as fast. That's slower than twice. So Maya covers more than a third.
at: So Maya covers more than a third

slides.say: One quarter is less than a third, so it's out.
Four ninths is left. And it fits, because a third is three ninths, and four ninths is more.
Choice number one is our answer, and I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number one is our answer
